chapter: Barnet, 52nd Street and New York recording dates
title: Bootleg recorders at Armstrong concerts in Europe
summary: In Europe from 1952 with Louis, pirates hid recording equipment in concert halls that the road manager could not find.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You know, when I was over there with Louis in Europe, they used to find trucks out in the back with all kind of electronic gadgets, picking up the whole concert, trucks full of electronic gadgets. They found a few, but how many got away with it? You know, you couldn't -- they were high on electronics many years ago over there, especially through Germany.

And they find means of recording. You couldn't keep them out. The road manager, Frenchy, he'd go looking for things of this sort, but he couldn't find it. You know, they had ways. They'd probably go in that concert hall and fix up things that he could never find, days before we'd give the concert.

All he had to do was pay a few bucks to some -- to somebody in the place to get in and do what they want to, put all kind of electric gadgets in there, you know. That's why you hear so many of those things over there.
That would have been in what, the '50's or what, '40's?

You mean in Europe when I was with Louis over there? No, that would have been in the '50's because I didn't go over with Louis until '52. You know, that would have been in the '50's. And we'd play an awful lot of concerts through Europe, you know, and naturally Louis played the best concert halls in Europe where the acoustics were perfect, you know, for doing things of this --

Yeah, were perfect, yeah. But you couldn't find these things. You know, you couldn't go around and find all you -- you were only in there for a day, and these guys have been there a week probably, setting up these things, you know.
